scope.summary: This standard prescribes the patterns, raw materials, construction, design shapes, standard dimensions, surface tolerances, physical-mechanical testing limits, and marking requirements for universal water closets (commercially known as Anglo-Indian combination closets) made of high-quality vitreous china.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). However, manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the prestigious physical 'ISI Mark' standard mark on the vitreous body of the water closet and its packaging box as a certified guarantee of chemical, mechanical, and thermal durability. Compliance with IS 2556 is strictly demanded in Public Works Department (PWD) contracts, municipal corporation building bylaws, and commercial construction projects across India.

requirements.detail: Under this 2024 revision, the standard explicitly aligns its technical and sanitary ware specifications with United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), supporting SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).

Universal water closets (commonly known as Anglo-Indian closets) must feature a dual-use design, allowing the toilet to be used as a sitting pedestal (EWC) or as a squatting pan (Indian style) using integrated raised non-slip footrests cast into the rim of the pan.

The fired body of the vitreous china sanitary appliance must be highly dense and vitrified, having an average water absorption limit not exceeding 0.5 percent of its dry mass, when evaluated using standard boiling and dry-weighing tests to prevent microbial ingress and odors.

The glaze must show zero cracks (crazing) when subjected to an autoclave steam-curing test at high pressure, guaranteeing that thermal expansion does not damage the glossy, impervious protective finish.
The integrated footrests on the universal WC rim must feature a highly textured or chequered non-slip pattern, designed to prevent foot slipping under wet conditions.
Universal closets fitted with P-trap or S-trap configurations must maintain an integrated water seal depth of not less than 50 mm, serving as a gas-tight barrier against toxic sewer vapors.
The closet must clear sawdust completely from the entire interior flushing rim area within a single flush cycle, ensuring a clean and hygienic pan surface.
Must be fully compatible with dual-flush siphonic or washdown systems, clearing toilet paper and standard artificial test solids using a water-saving flush volume of 6/3 litres or 4/2 litres.
If the manufacturer opts for additional water efficiency requirements, the product must be evaluated, rated, and marked with a standard water efficiency rating and labelling system.

Observed or calculated test dimensions, flush volumes, and clearances must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 2556 (Part 15) : 2024 (Third Revision) is the national Indian Standard specification establishing technical, design, and performance requirements for universal water closets (commonly known as Anglo-Indian combination closets) made of vitreous china. Formulated by the Sanitary Appliances and Accessories Subcommittee (CED 3:1) and published in May 2024, the standard unifies requirements for dual-use toilets that combine a sitting pedestal with integrated raised, anti-slip footrests for squatting. To support public health, sustainable water usage, and quality assurance, the standard enforces strict vitreous china physical testing (limiting water absorption to 0.5% and requiring crazing resistance), a minimum 50 mm water trap seal depth, highly efficient water-saving dual flushing limits (6/3 litres), and direct alignment with United Nations SDGs (SDG 6, SDG 11, and SDG 12).
